repo_notes.content: Lexicon (@ashlr/lexicon) is a TypeScript, Node.js and ESM personal lexicon that corrects speech-to-text transcripts before they reach agents. Source is the ground truth: src/core contains matching, storage and trust; src/cli and src/mcp expose it; src/hooks supplies Claude Code hooks. Explain data flow with diagrams and cite source files. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explains design decisions and docs/CONTRACT.md describes the public API.
Distinguish global and trusted project lexicons, and explain preview and explicit application for agent-initiated writes. Do not include secret values, personal transcripts or real machine paths.

Lexicon is one repo in the Ashlr.AI ecosystem: Phantom and its ecosystem form a fully autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory, run by agents with the human as a passive board member, chasing open source RSI (recursive self improvement). The other repos are Phantom, phantom-secrets, ashlr-plugin, Locus, ashlr-md and ashlr-stack; the README section 'Part of the Ashlr.AI ecosystem' gives each one's role. Lexicon runs without any of them. The tie is the companion handshake (docs/ashlr-handshake.md, src/cli/handshake.ts, src/cli/companions.ts): each tool answers --ashlr-handshake --json, and lexicon doctor reads Locus and ashlr-md that way. Do not describe features of the other repos beyond what this repo's docs state.

Agents write and ship this code. AGENTS.md is the entry point for any agent and CLAUDE.md is the working brief; CONTRIBUTING.md#contribute-with-an-agent is the contributor path (fork, npm ci, lexicon test-select, the CI Gate commands). A pull request has one required check, CI Gate (typecheck, build, crypto policy check, redaction test, diff secret scans); the merge queue reruns it and squash-merges with no approving review. Plugin bundle drift (npm run check:bundle) and stale doc counts (npm run check:facts) are caught only by the daily full suite on main. docs/CLI.md and fresh:-marked doc blocks are generated; never describe them as hand-written.

src/ambiguity/ (the ambiguity engine ported from Pellucid) is self-contained and nothing in src/ calls it yet; describe it as unwired, per docs/design/two-stage-correction.md. The Windows tray app (apps/windows) is built and unit-tested but has never been run on Windows (docs/WINDOWS-APP.md).
